record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: For k >= 5, determine whether there exist (2k + 2)-regular bar k-visibility graphs.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 21 Are there (2k + 2)-regular bar k-visibility graphs for k >= 5?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A bar representation is a finite collection $B = \{b_1, \dots, b_n\}$ of pairwise disjoint horizontal closed line segments (bars) in the plane, where no two bars are collinear. For a nonnegative integer $k$, the bar $k$-visibility graph of $B$ is the graph $G$ with vertex set $B$ in which two distinct bars $b_i$ and $b_j$ are adjacent if and only if there exists a vertical open line segment with one endpoint in $b_i$ and the other in $b_j$ that intersects at most $k$ other bars of $B$. A graph is called a bar $k$-visibility graph if it is isomorphic to the bar $k$-visibility graph of some bar representation. A graph is $d$-regular if every vertex has degree exactly $d$.

Determine, for each integer $k \ge 5$, whether there exists a $(2k+2)$-regular bar $k$-visibility graph.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem about bar k-visibility graphs. Existence of (2k+2)-regular bar k-visibility graphs is known for small k (k ≤ 4), but no source found in the search confirms a resolution for k ≥ 5.

status_evidence.title: Bar k-Visibility Graphs (Dean et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses regular bar k-visibility graphs; shows constraints on (2k+2)-regular cases.
status_evidence.claim: The (2k+2)-regular question is the natural threshold; non-complete regular bar k-visibility graphs of degree below 2k+2 do not exist.

status_evidence.title: A Study of Bar and Arc k-Visibility Graphs (PRIMES 2015)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys known results and open questions on bar k-visibility graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of (2k+2)-regular bar k-visibility graphs for k ≥ 5 is referenced as an open question in subsequent work.
